script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

Title: MENDING THE BROKEN LINK

INT. TECH COMPANY - DAY

A TECH COMPANY, PULSING WITH THE ENERGY OF INNOVATION. EMPLOYEES RUSH AROUND, WORKING ON LAPTOPS, TALKING INTO HEADSETS, AND SOLVING PROBLEMS.

INT. TECH COMPANY - HR OFFICE - DAY

JESSICA (30s, a sympathetic HR MANAGER) sits at her desk, going through files. The phone rings. She answers.

JESSICA:
HR. Jessica Speaking. How may I help you today?

CALLER (V.O.):
Hi, Jessica. It's me, Tom.

Jessica's eyes widen, and her smile fades as she recognizes the voice. She stands up, her hands shaking.

INT. TECH COMPANY - HR OFFICE - CONT'D

TOM (40s, a former coworker and now a disgruntled ex-employee) enters the HR office. He looks older and unshaven, with sad eyes.

JESSICA:
(stammering)
Tom. I wasn't expecting you. What can I do for you?

TOM:
I came to apologize. To ask for forgiveness.

Jessica looks surprised but also a little curious.

JESSICA:
(skeptical)
Why now, Tom? What changed?

Tom looks down, ashamed. He takes a deep breath and speaks.

TOM:
I lost my job a few months ago. I couldn't pay my bills, and I fell into a deep depression. I started drinking, and it got the best of me. I hurt so many people, including you. And I've been living with the guilt ever since.

Jessica listens intently, her expression softening.

JESSICA:
Tom, I understand that people make mistakes. And sometimes, those mistakes can lead us down a dark path. But it takes courage to acknowledge them and seek forgiveness.

Tom looks up, his eyes meeting Jessica's.

TOM:
I want to make things right. I want to come back to the company and make amends. I know I can't change the past, but I can learn from it and try to be a better person.

Jessica thinks for a moment before speaking.

JESSICA:
I'll consider it. But it won't be easy. You'll have to prove yourself to your former colleagues, and you'll need to show that you've changed. Do you understand that?

Tom nods, looking determined.

INT. TECH COMPANY - CAFETERIA - DAY

Tom works in the cafeteria, serving food to his former colleagues. They look at him with suspicion and disdain, but Tom remains humble and polite.

INT. TECH COMPANY - JESSICA'S OFFICE - DAY

Jessica and Tom sit in Jessica's office, discussing Tom's progress.

JESSICA:
Tom, it's been a few weeks now. How have things been going?

TOM:
It's been tough. People are still wary of me, and I can't blame them. But I'm trying to be patient and prove myself. I've been attending AA meetings, and I'm seeing a therapist. I've also been volunteering in the community.

Jessica smiles, impressed.

JESSICA:
That's great to hear, Tom. Keep up the good work.

INT. TECH COMPANY - CAFETERIA - DAY

Tom serves food to his colleagues, who have started to warm up to him. One by one, they start to offer him words of encouragement and even friendship.

INT. TECH COMPANY - HR OFFICE - DAY

Jessica sits at her desk, reflecting on Tom's progress. She hears a knock on the door. It's Tom.

TOM:
Jessica, may I come in?

Jessica looks up, pleased to see Tom's progress.

JESSICA:
Of course, Tom. Come in.

Tom looks nervous but determined.

TOM:
I'd like to ask for your forgiveness, Jessica. Forgiveness for my past mistakes and for any hurt I may have caused you.

Jessica looks at Tom, her expression soft and understanding.

JESSICA:
Tom, I've seen the effort you've put into changing yourself. And I believe that people deserve a second chance. So yes, Tom, I forgive you.

Tom looks relieved and grateful, his eyes welling up with tears.

TOM:
Thank you, Jessica. I won't let you down again.

Jessica smiles and pats Tom on the shoulder.

JESSICA:
I have faith in you, Tom. And I'll be here to support you every step of the way.

INT. TECH COMPANY - DAY

Tom walks through the tech company, feeling a sense of belonging and purpose. He looks around at his colleagues, who now greet him with smiles and nods. Tom realizes that forgiveness is a powerful thing, and that it's never too late to make things right.

FADE OUT.

END OF SCREENPLAY.
